result.summary: This PR adds interfaces::Wallet::deriveHDKey(), backed by a new CWallet::DeriveHDKey() method that consolidates the HD key selection and derivation logic previously inlined in the derivehdkey RPC. The RPC is refactored to call the new wallet method instead of duplicating the checks, which changes several of its error codes (moving -8 and -5 cases to -4) while keeping the watch-only (-4) and locked-wallet (-13) codes unchanged. Only the derived xpub and its key origin cross the interface; private key material does not. It follows the same pattern as the already-merged #35436 (addHDKey) and #34861 (importdescriptors interface), all feeding the Multisig Wizard project (#35645).
result.problem: The derivehdkey RPC (#32784) lets a user derive an xpub from an HD key at an arbitrary path, but the GUI does not go through RPC, so this capability is unreachable from the GUI. Multisig wallet setup in the GUI needs a way to derive and display a shareable xpub, which this interface provides.

open_concerns: Whether collapsing several derivehdkey RPC error codes into -4 breaks compatibility for callers relying on the v32 error contract (pseudoramdom, tagging achow101 for a decision); author has offered to duplicate checks to preserve old codes if needed

resolved_concerns: achow101's objection to duplicating derivation logic between RPC and interface was resolved by making both call the same CWallet::DeriveHDKey
jeanpablojp's concern that unit tests could pass even with a wrong derived key was fixed by comparing against the wallet's own active HD key
Reachability of a dead-code branch (locked-wallet check) flagged by jeanpablojp/polespinasa was removed

result.card: This PR adds interfaces::Wallet::deriveHDKey(), backed by a consolidated CWallet::DeriveHDKey(), so the GUI can derive and display a shareable xpub from an HD key without going through RPC, as part of the tracked Multisig Wizard project (#35645) alongside the already-merged addHDKey interface (#35436). It refactors the existing derivehdkey RPC to share the same logic, which changes some of its error codes from -8/-5 to -4, a compatibility question pseudoramdom raised as unresolved since the RPC already shipped in v32. Three reviewers (polespinasa, jeanpablojp, pseudoramdom) gave concept ACKs, and a maintainer's duplication objection was resolved by unifying the RPC and interface implementation. The commit structure is still being actively reworked per a detailed proposal from polespinasa, and the error-contract question awaits a decision. No fund-safety risk since only the derived xpub, not private key material, crosses the interface.
